results.title: Photoplethysmography (PPG) - News-Medical.Net
results.content: Since light is more strongly absorbed by blood than the surrounding tissues, the changes in blood flow can be detected by PPG sensors as changes in the intensity of light. A PPG signal has several components including volumetric changes in arterial blood which is associated with cardiac activity, variations in venous blood volume which modulates the PPG signal, a DC component showing the tissues’ optical property and subtle energy changes in the body. PPG shows the blood flow changes as a waveform with the help of a bar or a graph. Medical devices based on PPG technology are widely used in various applications in the clinical set up. These intensity changes are associated with changes in blood flow through the tissue and provide vital cardiovascular information such as the pulse rate. Researchers have studied skin blood flow and the related rhythms using a near infrared CCD PPG imaging system. https://www.news-medical.net/health/Photoplethysmography-(PPG).aspx.
